Here's a description of the provided plot, following your guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relative change in percentage for different configurations of layer sizes and token counts. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and represents layer numbers, with a linear scale ranging from Layer1-4 to Layer29-32, with tick labels at each layer. The y-axis is labeled “Relative Change” and represents percentage change, with a linear scale ranging from -25% to 5%, with tick labels at 5% intervals. There are five lines displayed on the plot. The first line is yellow, marked with circular data points, and labeled “LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit”; it begins at approximately 1.5% at Layer1-4, declines to approximately -13% at Layer13-20, and ends at approximately -12% at Layer29-32. The second line is red, marked with square data points, and labeled “LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit”; it begins at approximately 0.5% at Layer1-4, declines to approximately -17% at Layer13-20, and ends at approximately -15% at Layer29-32. The third line is olive, marked with circular data points, and labeled “RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit”; it begins at approximately 2.5% at Layer1-4, declines to approximately -14% at Layer13-20, and ends at approximately -13% at Layer29-32. The fourth line is blue, marked with square data points, and labeled “RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit”; it begins at approximately 1% at Layer1-4, declines to approximately -24% at Layer13-20, and ends at approximately -22% at Layer29-32. Finally, there is a gray dashed line labeled “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit”, which remains relatively constant at approximately 0% across all layer values.
